# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges constrained by numeric cell clues
- **Mid-loop** – Loop where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop alternating between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through white circles with straight/turn rules per region; avoids black circles
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order

#### Loop with Cell Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop drawn while placing black cells indicated by arrow clues

### B. Path/Connection Drawing (Non-loop)
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with 1–2 bridges; all islands connected

### C. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors certain cells black (or leaves them white).

#### Shading with Numeric Clues about Adjacent/Nearby Black Cells
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs; numbered black squares constrain adjacent bulb count; illumination coverage required
- **Kurotto** – Circle numbers indicate sum of contiguous black cell groups touching the circle
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers count visible white cells in four directions to nearest black cell or edge
- **Usowan** – Numbers count adjacent black cells, but one number per room is wrong
- **Shakashaka** – Place diagonal triangles in cells; remaining white areas must be rectangles; numbers count adjacent triangles

#### Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Rooms with numbers dictating black cell count; white connectivity and no 3-room white spans
- **Norinori** – Each bold-lined region gets exactly two black cells forming dominoes
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white promontories; no 2×2 of either color; white connected
- **Nurimeizu** – Paint entire rooms to create a maze from S to G with path constraints
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; connected shading, no 2×2, no same-shape adjacency
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms (number gives count); when "dropped" by gravity, fill bottom half
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles; diagonal-cell numbers constrain black cell counts in rows/columns
- **Choco Banana** – Black cell groups must be rectangles; white cell groups must not be rectangles; numbers give group size

#### Shading by Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no repeats in rows/columns; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected

### D. Region Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into blocks or regions.

#### Division with Size Constraints
- **Shikaku** – Divide into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide into pentominoes; numbers count surrounding block edges (including frame)
- **Fillomino** – Fill numbers and partition into polyominoes; block size equals its number; same-size blocks can't touch

#### Division with Shape Constraints
- **Sashigane** – Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark endpoints
- **Double Choco** – Divide so each block has matching white and gray regions of identical shape

### E. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### Latin-Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition

#### Regional Number Filling
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; same numbers in a line must be spaced apart ≥ the number's value
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrows in black cells point to the largest neighbor; no same-number adjacency across rooms

#### Number List Placement
- **Nansuke** – Place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-style grid

### F. Object Placement/Movement

#### Placement of Objects
- **Akari** (also shading) – Place light bulbs with illumination and adjacency rules
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (sequences 1–5) with no touching and line-of-sight attack constraints
- **Chained Block** – Determine black cells forming blocks; blocks must chain diagonally; unique shapes per chain
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips of specified length

#### Movement of Objects
- **Satogaeri** – Move numbered circles specified distances so each country has exactly one
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; gray area sums must match

### G. Symbol Filling (Non-numeric)
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; limited consecutive same-orientation runs

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
- White cells must be connected: **Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Usowan**
- Black/shaded cells must be connected: **Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin**
- All islands connected by bridges: **Hashiwokakero**

### No 2×2 Constraints
- No 2×2 black: **Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu**
- No 2×2 of either color: **Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu**

### Adjacency Prohibition (Black-Black)
- No horizontally/vertically adjacent black cells: **Hitori, Heyawake, Akari (bulb-to-bulb), Yajilin, Usowan, Kurodoko**

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
- **Akari** (illumination rays), **Kurodoko** (white cell counting), **Hebi** (snake attack sight lines)

### Room/Region-Based Clues
- **Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Double Choco, Five Cells, Sto-stone, Usowan, Juosan**

### Directional/Arrow Clues
- **Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Sashigane, Nagareru, Evolomino, Pencils, Yosenabe**

---

## III. By Grid Element Used for Clues

### Numeric Clues in Cells
**Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Five Cells, Fillomino, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Makaro, Nansuke, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Ripple Effect, Satogaeri, Shakashaka, Shikaku, Slitherlink, Sto-stone, Sudoku, Suraromu, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin, Yosenabe**

### Circle Clues (Black/White)
**Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Hashiwokakero, Nurimisaki, Kurotto, Satogaeri, Sashigane, Suraromu, Yosenabe**

### Arrow Clues
**Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Sashigane, Evolomino, Nagareru**

### Bold-Line Regions
**Heyawake, Double Choco, Dotchi-Loop, Five Cells, Makaro, Moon-or-Sun, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Ripple Effect, Satogaeri, Sto-stone, Suraromu, Tilepaint, Usowan, Juosan**

### Moon/Sun Symbols
**Moon-or-Sun**

### Question Marks
**Chained Block**

---

## IV. By Output Type

| Output | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Single closed loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Non-crossing paths** | Numberlink |
| **Bridges between nodes** | Hashiwokakero |
| **Lines from objects** | Pencils |
| **Binary cell coloring** | Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin |
| **Region partition** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Fillomino, Sashigane, Double Choco |
| **Number placement** | Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Fillomino |
| **Symbol placement** | Juosan (— or \|), Hebi (snake numbers), Evolomino (squares) |
| **Object movement** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
